annotation.title_clean: A Review of - Humans and Robots: Ethics, Agency, and Anthromorphism by Sven Nyholm
annotation.title_en: A Review of - Humans and Robots: Ethics, Agency, and Anthropomorphism by Sven Nyholm
annotation.venue: Journal of Ethics and Emerging Technologies
annotation.summary_en: Book review of Sven Nyholm's 'Humans and Robots', which examines the ethics of human-robot interaction, robot agency and anthropomorphism. The reviewer praises the framework but notes the human/robot distinction is underspecified. The review discusses how legal notions of agency and responsibility fit robotic agency.
key_provisions_or_claims: Ethics of human-robot interaction treats humans and robots as two-way agents subject to normative considerations.
Robot agency is a kind in its own right and should not be judged by human-agency standards.
Humans are prone to anthropomorphize robots because psychology and institutions evolved before robots.
Legal notions of agency do not map neatly onto robotic agency, complicating responsibility attribution.
The distinction between humans and humanoid robots is insufficiently defined, limiting generalizability.
